hook: SCP-3017 begins as a file on a dangerous criminal who can't be kept behind bars, and the Foundation's methods for holding him grow harsher as the document goes on. Notice that both the procedures and the description appear twice, one version marked as updated and the other as void. Content note: coercive interrogation, a family killed in a fire, and suicide.
whyItMatters: The horror here is aimed at the people doing the containing rather than at the subject. Hostage-taking is written up in the flat vocabulary of incentives and mitigation, and the dry format makes it feel almost routine until one researcher starts asking where the evidence is. It shows how the standard report structure can be used to indict the institution that writes it.
thingsToNotice: The truth is that the anomaly was never his criminality but the compulsion others felt to lock him up, and only the people closest to him were immune. Rylan's memo finds no real evidence of any crime and she is contained for raising it, while the grandmother's cancer and the shooting of his ex-partner turn out to be lies used to break him. After Rylan helps him escape, his family home burns in what is ruled arson, killing his relatives, his fiancee and a neighbour, and he is found dead, believed to have jumped from a bridge, even as Rylan insists he did not want to die. Dr. Kiran's unexplained absence covers those same dates. The updated procedures treat continued interest in this very file as a symptom, and the page closes by warning you not to leave it open.
